newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pakistan cargo airline to launch Europe service.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cargo airline to launch Europe service.

text.p: Pakistan cargo airline Shaheen Air Cargo said it will launch a Europe freighter service on May 26 to meet growing air cargo export demand.
Mohammad Shamim, the airline's western Europe general manager, said Shaheen Air Cargo would operate a weekly Boeing 707 freighter service offering 40 tonnes' capacity between Lahore and Ostend.
The service would be doubled to twice weekly if demand proved sufficient, he told Reuters in an interview.
"Pakistan is opening up and PIA (Pakistan International Airlines) cannot offer enough capacity, which is why it is the right time to start this service," he said.
"Lahore is the main freight hub in Pakistan and flights will be full from Pakistan. It is a question of how much we can fly back (from Europe)," he added.
The Lahore market was currently generating about 400 tonnes of export air cargo a week, mostly textiles and leather goods, Shamim said.
A good share of this was presently carried on twice-weekly Lufthansa Cargo Boeing 727F flights to Sharjah and transhipped on to Frankfurt, he noted.
In Europe, trucking services to and from the Shaheen freighter would be managed by freight forwarder LEP International, Shamim said.
Shaheen Air Cargo is a subsidiary of the Pakistan Air Force-owned business group Shaheen Foundation and a sister company of Shaheen Airlines International.
It has operated ad-hoc cargo charter flights to and from CIS states and has flown Pakistani UN soldiers to several countries in recent years, Shamim said.
